title: The Best Early Black Friday iPad Deals Already Worth Shopping
gist: Wired's early Black Friday iPad roundup notes 2026 was a slow year for Apple tablets: only the iPad Air and iPad Mini were updated and the whole lineup took a $100–$200 price hike in June. Discounts are modest ($50–$100), the previous-gen 2024 iPad Mini at $499 is called the best deal, and the iPad Pro has not been discounted at all.

themes.theme: Apple iPad lineup cadence and pricing in 2026

insights.claim: In 2026 Apple updated only the iPad Air and iPad Mini, leaving the base iPad and iPad Pro unchanged since 2025.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Signals a slower iPad refresh cycle, a soft driver for Apple's tablet revenue in 2026.
insights.quote: There's no denying that 2026 has been a slower year for the iPad lineup.

insights.claim: Apple raised prices across the entire iPad lineup in June 2026 by either $100 or $200 depending on the model.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Lineup-wide price hikes point to cost pressure or margin defense at Apple and may dampen unit demand.
insights.quote: in June, the entire lineup was subject to a painful price hike of either $100 or $200, depending on the model

insights.claim: Despite being released only a month earlier, the 2026 iPad Mini with an OLED display is already discounted $100 to $599 ahead of Black Friday.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Early discounting on a brand-new model can hint at softer demand or aggressive retailer promotion.

insights.claim: The 11-inch iPad Pro has not been discounted at all for Black Friday 2026 and remains $1,099, cheaper than the 13-inch MacBook Air that uses the same M5 chip, though the Magic Keyboard must be bought separately.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Holding price on the flagship suggests Apple protecting premium-tier margins during promotions.
insights.quote: It's a little surprising that the iPad Pro hasn't been discounted at all for Black Friday.

insights.claim: Wired argues the two-year-old 2024 iPad Mini at $499 is a better buy for most people than the newer 2026 model, which costs $300 more despite its OLED screen and thinner chassis.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Older models cannibalizing newer ones at holiday prices may weaken the mix shift toward pricier new hardware.
insights.quote: most people should stick with the older model
insights.locator: Even though it's more than two years old

insights.claim: Wired recommends the M4 iPad Air as the iPad to buy for work because it pairs a powerful chip with Magic Keyboard trackpad support and newer iPadOS versions make windowing and the cursor more macOS-like.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: iPadOS converging with macOS blurs the line between iPad and Mac sales, affecting Apple's product mix.
insights.quote: I find that it's the iPad people should buy if they intend to use it for work
insights.locator: The iPad Air is the in-between iPad.

insights.claim: Pre-Black Friday iPad discounts in 2026 are shallow, with the base iPad cut just $50 to $399 and the iPad Air $100 to $649, prices described as fairly common rather than rare.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Shallow discounts suggest limited promotional pressure on Apple pricing this holiday season.
